papers.title: A Superconducting Phase Transition Single-Electron Transistor
papers.abstract: Quantum computers require fast and accurate methods for qubit state detection. Phase-transition sensors exploit the abrupt change between two physical states of a material to achieve enhanced sensitivity and have enabled advanced detectors for quantum technologies, such as superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. However, this sensing principle has not yet been applied to semiconductor spin qubits. Here, we demonstrate a superconducting phase-transition radio-frequency single-electron transistor (PTSET), a charge sensor for semiconductor spin qubits whose response is enhanced by a superconducting-to-normal phase transition. The transition is engineered by linking the sensor current to a low-critical-current, high-kinetic-inductance inductor integrated into the radio-frequency matching network. We demonstrate improvements in sensitivity of one and two orders of magnitude over conventional rfSETs in the large- and small-signal regimes, respectively. Our results establish phase-transition sensing as a route towards ultrasensitive, integrated charge sensors for semiconductor quantum computing and point to broader applications, including cryogenic photon detection for radio astronomy.

summary.summary: The work demonstrates a superconducting phase-transition radio-frequency single-electron transistor (PTSET) that exploits a superconducting-to-normal phase transition in a high-kinetic-inductance TiN inductor to enhance charge sensing sensitivity for semiconductor spin qubits. The device achieves one order of magnitude improvement in the large-signal regime and two orders of magnitude in the small-signal regime compared to conventional rfSETs.
summary.motivation: Semiconductor spin qubits require fast and accurate charge readout to enable rapid error correction cycles, and phase-transition sensors offer a route to enhanced sensitivity by operating near a material phase transition where small perturbations produce large macroscopic changes.
summary.method: A 22-nm CMOS integrated circuit with a TiN superconducting thin film (3 nm thick, $L_K = 122$ nH, $T_c = 1.1$ K) tuned via 0.6 T out-of-plane magnetic field to $I_c \sim 33$ nA is connected in series with a silicon-on-insulator FET-based SET. Charge sensing events modulate the tunneling current through the SET to trigger the phase transition, abruptly changing the circuit impedance from inductive to resistive ($R_{\mathrm{norm}} = 75$ kΩ).
summary.result: In the small-signal regime typical of spin readout, minimum integration time $t_{\mathrm{min}}$ drops by nearly two orders of magnitude when operating across the phase transition (at $V_{\mathrm{DS}} = -7.5$ mV) compared to conventional rfSET mode; theoretical modeling predicts SNR improvement factors exceeding 350 for well-overcoupled designs ($\beta = 10$), with recovery times estimated at 10–100 ns based on TiN superconducting gap.

papers.title: A 12-CNOT Double Qubit Excitation Gate
papers.abstract: Effective implementation of high-level quantum gates is essential for practical quantum computing. In this work, we presented, to the best of our knowledge, the first reported 12-CNOT decomposition of the double qubit excitation operator. We compared our new circuit with the previous SOTA 13-CNOT circuits in 4 different metrics. Our new circuit has the lowest CNOT count (12), lowest CNOT depth (8, roughly 27% reduction), and lowest total circuit depth (15, 25% reduction) among all the previous SOTA circuits. With output qubit relabeling, the CNOT depth can be further reduced to 7 (roughly 36% reduction from 11). Further, we only added 2 extra 1q gates (from 11 to 13) compared to the best of the SOTA circuits. As the double qubit excitation operator can be used as a building block hundreds or thousands of times in practical quantum algorithms, any reduction in such primitives compounds over the full circuit, resulting in significant overall resource savings.

summary.summary: This work presents the first 12-CNOT decomposition of the double-qubit excitation operator $U^{ij}_{kl}(\theta) = \exp[-i\theta/8(\sum_m c_m P_m)]$, which rotates between computational basis states $|0011\rangle$ and $|1100\rangle$. The new circuit improves upon state-of-the-art 13-CNOT implementations with reduced CNOT depth (8, ∼27% reduction; 7 with output relabeling, ∼36% reduction) and total circuit depth (15, ∼25% reduction).
summary.motivation: The double-qubit excitation operator serves as a fundamental building block in near-term variational algorithms like VQE with UCCSD ansätze and in fault-tolerant algorithms for electronic-structure Hamiltonian simulation and quantum phase estimation, so reducing its resource footprint compounds over hundreds or thousands of uses.
summary.method: Using systematic exploration with circuit synthesis tools (Q-Synth, Qiskit Transpiler, Tket) and techniques including Clifford synthesis and CNOT+$R_z$ synthesis, a 12-CNOT circuit was discovered that improves upon the previous SOTA approach of absorbing CNOTs from $L$ and $R$ transformation circuits into the $C_3R_y$ rotation decomposition.
summary.result: The 12-CNOT circuit (Figure 5) achieves CNOT depth 8 with 13 single-qubit gates and total depth 15; with output-wire relabeling (Figure 6) CNOT depth reduces to 7 while maintaining 12 CNOT count and total depth 15, compared to Nam's 13-CNOT best-previous with CNOT depth 13 and depth 22.
